page: Amazon Web Services inf1.2xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform features an Intel Xeon 8275CL x86_64 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz across 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs, supported by 35 MB of L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB per virtual core. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single AWS Inferentia chip equipped with 8 GB of total VRAM. The instance does not include local disk storage and connects with a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent middle-tier host CPU performance alongside specialized accelerator metrics. The host system achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1211.0 and a multi-core score of 4565.0, paired with a PassMark CPU score of 8870.98. Memory throughput reaches 50.99 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 38.4 GB/sec for large-block writes. For machine learning tasks, the single Inferentia accelerator yields 117.52 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M parameter model, but performance declines on larger architectures, recording 11.45 tokens per second prompt processing and 6.67 tokens per second text generation on a 7B parameter model.

The absence of integrated local storage necessitates network-attached storage solutions, which rely on the 5 Gbps baseline network link. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance targets specialized inference pipelines where deploying full-scale discrete GPUs would introduce resource and cost overheads. The hardware profile is aligned with lightweight machine learning inference, computer vision, natural language text processing, and associated microservices.
